note: The spec's worked example (section 2): the pull request title in a shell, node:latest, curl | bash and the tj-actions pin into ci/build, which holds a read token and no secret and saves nothing, so every path there is code execution alone on an ephemeral runner, Low, one per subject (the forbidden tag and the missing digest of node:latest anchor one path together). The tj-actions pin is a full commit SHA: offline the advisory is not fetched, and the unauthorized source alone is no entry (nothing changes without a commit here), so it is an other finding at High; with the advisory it would anchor a High path, the unauthorized source joining it. plumber.yml runs on push to main with id-token: write and security-events: write: a write token, but no signing or release step, so no impact, and the unprotected main anchors an unprotected_push path into it that is High (a token, no impact) and could never be Critical (a push entry is capped at High). The getplumber/plumber action is SHA-pinned from a default trusted owner, so it anchors nothing. Hand count: one High path (the unprotected_push path) 15, three Low paths (the pull request title, node:latest and the fetched script into ci/build) 3 x 3 = 9, one other finding, the unauthorized source at Medium 5 (the persisted credentials on plumber/plumber ride the push path), so 100 - 29 = 71, no Critical path: B.
